ordered_step_reconstruction: On an internal opposite-label cell, signed normalization by u_i=U(t_i) gives f(0)=g(0)=1 and f(theta)=z, g(theta)=-z even when u_i is negative. Exact oscillator propagation yields x=(z-c)/s, y=(-z-C)/S, x_R=(cz-1)/(sz), and y_R=(1+Cz)/(Sz). The normalized common energy is x^2-y^2=(1-q^2)/(rho u_i^2)<0.

For h=f^2-g^2, the two inward switching derivatives are controlled by x-mu y and x_R-mu y_R. With t=tan(theta/2), T=tan(mu theta/2), D=mu T^2t+Tt^2+T+mu t and N=mu T^2t-Tt^2+T-mu t, direct reduction gives x-mu y=[D/(2Tt)](z-k) and x_R-mu y_R=-[D/(2Tt)](1-kz)/z, k=N/D.

The identity N/(Tt)=2[cot(theta)-mu cot(mu theta)] is positive because x cot x strictly decreases on (0,pi), while D-N=2t(Tt+mu)>0. Hence 0<k<1 before branch selection. The two strict endpoint orientations then exhaust all amplitude cases: a positive cell has z>0 and k<z<1/k, whereas a negative cell has z<0.

Writing r=(T-t)/(T+t), independent symbolic expansion verifies x^2-y^2=(Tt-1)(Tt+1)(t^2-T^2)(z-r)(z-1/r)/(4T^2t^2) and k-r=2Tt(mu-1)(Tt-1)/[(T+t)D]. For a positive cell Tt>1 would put its switch interval strictly inside the positive-energy interval (r,1/r), contradicting negative energy; equality gives zero energy. Thus Tt<1. For z<0 the root factors have positive product, so negative energy gives Tt>1.

Since theta/2 and mu theta/2 both lie in (0,pi/2), tan(theta/2)tan(mu theta/2) is less than, equal to, or greater than one exactly when (mu+1)theta is less than, equal to, or greater than pi. Strict energy excludes equality. Therefore positive internal cells have 0<theta<pi/(mu+1), while negative internal cells have pi/(mu+1)<theta<pi/mu.

The accepted odd-positive/even-negative internal allocation yields max_odd theta_i<pi/(mu+1)<min_even theta_i and the alternating adjacent order. Endpoint cells are not opposite-label internal cells and receive only the existing R6 upper bound. No reflection property or finite computation enters the derivation.

ordered_step_reconstruction: For F_mu(theta)=sin(theta)/[sin(theta)+mu sin(mu theta)], direct differentiation equals mu sin(theta)sin(mu theta)[cot(theta)-mu cot(mu theta)] divided by a positive square. Hence F_mu is strictly increasing on 0<theta<pi/mu. The new phase separation therefore orients each chi_(i-1)-chi_i, chi=(q^2-1)F_mu.

Exact material-time translation, cell Dirichlet-to-Neumann identities, and saltation telescope to M gamma=(q^2-chi_1, chi_1-chi_2, ..., chi_(m-2)-chi_(m-1), -r_L^2+chi_(m-1)). The boundary terms are 1+(q^2-1)(1-F_mu(theta_1))>0 and -p_L^2-(q^2-1)(1-F_mu(theta_(m-1)))<0. Thus every component of M gamma has the same strict sign as gamma.

The diagonal signature gauge e_(i+1)/e_i=sign(K_i) turns M into a symmetric irreducible Jacobi matrix J_0 with strictly negative off-diagonals. The gauged vector g has sign pattern (+,-,-,+,+,-,-,+,...) and exactly n sign changes among m=2n nonzero entries.

Set r_i=(J_0g)_i/g_i>0 and H=J_0-diag(r_i). Then Hg=0. The finite three-term characteristic-polynomial recurrence gives simple eigenvalues, strict interlacing, and the sign-change index; zero is the (n+1)-st eigenvalue in increasing order. Therefore In(H)=(n-1 positive,n negative,1 zero). Strict positive diagonal addition gives lambda_(n+1)(J_0)>0 and n_-(M)<=n.

For max, L_0=B^T K^(-1)B has inertia (n positive,n-1 negative,1 zero), since B is onto with one-dimensional constant kernel and K has n positive and n-1 negative entries. A maximal negative subspace plus that kernel is n-dimensional and becomes strictly negative under M=L_0-D, D>0. Hence n_-(M)>=n. Together with the strict upper comparison, In(M)=(n positive,n negative,0 zero).

For G=[-D,B^T;B,-K], Schur complementation through -K gives In(G)=In(-K)+In(M)=(2n-1 positive,2n negative,0 zero). Schur complementation through -D gives In(G)=In(-D)+In(BD^(-1)B^T-K). Consequently the (2n-1)-dimensional physical path matrix L_+=BD^(-1)B^T-K is positive definite.

The exact relative recurrence yields M d=(-w_0,0,...,0,w_m)^T. For the log(q) field, w_0=0 and d_1=-1; the corner cofactor of tridiagonal M gives w_m=-det(M)product_i K_i, with polynomial continuant continuation covering singular coefficient tuples. Since sign det(M)=(-1)^n and sign product K_i=(-1)^(n-1), w_m>0 for max.

The accepted R7 terminal bridge then yields det(L_+)>0, J<0, and partial_q A_n>0 in the relative scaling quotient. This conclusion is pointwise at every transverse common-terminal max root. It does not connect chambers, control nongeneric closures, prove fixed-mu global order, solve the equal-norm residual, or establish O3a.
